label: Continuous urban fabric
notes: Sealed surface, vegetation below the mapping unit.

label: Discontinuous urban fabric
notes: The wildland-urban interface itself. Gardens, hedges and unmanaged plots inside it do carry fire, and this is where exposure assessment matters most -- but the class records buildings, not fuel. Treated as non-fuel here and as an ASSET in fev_vuln_layer(), which is the honest split.

label: Industrial or commercial units
notes: Sealed or bare surface.

label: Road and rail networks and associated land
notes: Linear infrastructure. Acts as a fuel break at this resolution, and as an ignition corridor in reality -- the mask records the first, not the second.

label: Port areas
notes: Sealed surface.

label: Airports
notes: Runways are non-fuel but airport grassland can be extensive. Below the mapping unit, so not separable.

label: Mineral extraction sites
notes: Bare mineral surface.

label: Dump sites
notes: Not vegetation fuel.

label: Construction sites
notes: Bare ground.

label: Green urban areas
notes: Parks and cemeteries: real vegetation, but irrigated, fragmented and managed. Burnable TRUE, with a low availability weight, rather than excluded outright.

label: Sport and leisure facilities
notes: Golf courses, campsites, leisure parks. Campsites embedded in maquis are a recurring casualty in Mediterranean fires, which is the reason this row is not FALSE.

label: Non-irrigated arable land
notes: See the note on agriculture above. Stubble carries fire for a few weeks a year; the mask has no season.

label: Permanently irrigated land
notes: Irrigated, kept green.

label: Rice fields
notes: Flooded for most of the cycle.

label: Vineyards
notes: Worked vine rows are near-inert and are used as fire breaks; abandoned ones are not.

label: Fruit trees and berry plantations
notes: Same reasoning as vineyards.

label: Olive groves
notes: The weakest FALSE in this table. Abandoned Mediterranean olive groves with a grass or shrub floor burn readily, and abandonment is widespread. Override this row for a Mediterranean study area where groves are not actively worked.

label: Pastures
notes: Grazed grassland: fine fuel, but kept short by stock. A pasture left ungrazed is functionally class 321.

label: Annual crops associated with permanent crops
notes: See the note on agriculture.

label: Complex cultivation patterns
notes: Small-holding mosaic. Contains hedges, field margins and fallow below the 25 ha unit, none of which are separable.

label: Land principally occupied by agriculture, with significant areas of natural vegetation
notes: The class is defined by containing significant natural vegetation, so the burnable fraction is real but unquantified -- somewhere between a quarter and a half of the polygon by the nomenclature's own definition. Burnable TRUE with a fractional availability weight is the least wrong option.

label: Agro-forestry areas
notes: Dehesa and montado: scattered oaks over grazed grass. Structurally an open forest, and it burns as one.

label: Broad-leaved forest
notes: Broadleaf forest. Cannot separate evergreen sclerophyll from deciduous -- holm oak and beech land in the same class. This single limitation is the strongest argument for keeping BD Forêt primary in France.

label: Coniferous forest
notes: Coniferous forest, species unresolved.

label: Mixed forest
notes: Mixed forest.

label: Natural grassland
notes: Ungrazed or lightly grazed grassland. One of the three classes CORINE is kept for.

label: Moors and heathland
notes: Moor and heath. One of the three classes CORINE is kept for.

label: Sclerophyllous vegetation
notes: Maquis and garrigue. The most important class CORINE contributes: highly flammable, extensive around the Mediterranean, and outside the BD Forêt's forest scope in places.

label: Transitional woodland-shrub
notes: Regeneration, encroachment and post-disturbance shrub. Given its own type because it is a transient state -- what it was at the CLC vintage is not what it is now, and the gap grows with the age of the vintage.

label: Beaches, dunes, sands
notes: Mostly bare, but back-dune vegetation exists below the mapping unit.

label: Bare rocks
notes: Rock. A genuine fuel break.

label: Sparsely vegetated areas
notes: Under 50% vegetation cover by definition, so fuel is present but discontinuous. Burnable TRUE with a low weight; spread across it is unreliable in either direction.

label: Burnt areas
notes: Burnt at the CLC vintage. Whether it is fuel today depends entirely on how long ago that was: bare in year one, and in Mediterranean shrubland among the most flammable states there is by year five to ten. Compare the CLC vintage to your analysis date before trusting this row.

label: Glaciers and perpetual snow
notes: Ice and snow.

label: Inland marshes
notes: Waterlogged, but reedbeds burn fast and hot when dry -- Camargue-type situations are not covered by this FALSE.

label: Peat bogs
notes: Peat burns by smouldering, which is a different process from the flaming spread this package models. FALSE is a scope decision, not a claim that peat does not burn.

label: Salt marshes
notes: Halophytic, waterlogged.

label: Salines
notes: Salt pans.

label: Intertidal flats
notes: Tidal, unvegetated.

label: Water courses
notes: Water.

label: Water bodies
notes: Water.

label: Coastal lagoons
notes: Water.

label: Estuaries
notes: Water.

label: Sea and ocean
notes: Water.
